cities: No store of its own in the US · its own site, and independent shops

craft_evidence.owned: Yes: own knitwear factory, Manchester, est. 2012, fully fashioned 7 and 5 gauge machines (brand own words "Our very own knitwear factory"); press repeats it owns it. Claim plus press, no filing seen. Other categories made by unowned suppliers.
craft_evidence.makers: No company names; product pages name only town and supplier history (Smethwick wax-jacket/tee factory est. 1978; Wolverhampton polo maker 50+ yrs; Leicester polo maker; Barcelona shirt workshop founded 1930; Porto soft tailoring; London wool coats). Only named company: Abraham Moon & Sons (blankets, not men's clothing).
craft_evidence.mills: NONE for men's clothing (only Abraham Moon & Sons, Yorkshire, 1837, for blankets); Montfort knitting mill named in 1796 history only.
craft_evidence.madein: 100% of 71 men's product pages (69 clothing) carry a "Made in" line: 54 UK (30 Manchester knitwear incl gloves, wax/tees Smethwick, polos Wolverhampton/Leicester, coats London), 10 Portugal, 5 Spain (Barcelona).
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed: Thomas Glover 1796, Wigston Magna near Leicester, hand-frame knitter; Peregrine brand name 1956 (Donald Glover); eight generations; King's Award for Enterprise (International Trade) 2025.
craft_evidence.process: Partial: Manchester factory page names fully fashioned 7 and 5 gauge machines, Merino and British wool; little process detail for other categories.
craft_evidence.reasoning: Owns its Manchester knitwear factory (est. 2012; about 30 of 69 styles) and has a dated, placed 1796 family history, and every product page states country. Not a 5: the rest (wax, tees, polos, Portugal tailoring, Spanish shirts) is bought in from unnamed suppliers, no men's mills are named, and the site says "all our clothing is still made right here in the UK" while 15 styles are Portugal/Spain.

ownership.owner: The Glover family, now in its eighth generation; Tom Glover is managing director.
